# Act IV: Geography & Authorship

*Where is the research about, and who produces it?*  Variables: country (190), income, UN region, `multi_country`; affiliation country + **institution**. **Extracted-geo only for income comparisons** (audit finding 17).

---

<div class="figure-card">
  <img src="../figures/fig_dotmap.png" alt="C15 Global dot map">
  <div class="figure-title">C15 — Global Proportional-Symbol Map</div>
  <div class="figure-meta">
    <span class="figure-badge badge-hero">★★★ Hero</span>
    <span class="figure-script">R/fig-companion-dotmap.R</span>
  </div>
  <div class="figure-description">Berrang-Ford style dot map: country counts, bubbles by income, Robinson projection. Where is the evidence on a map?</div>
  <div class="figure-finding">Evidence concentrated in North America, Western Europe, East Asia. Africa and South Asia visible but sparse. Dot size = study count, colour = income.</div>
</div>

<div class="figure-card">
  <img src="../figures/fig_burden.png" alt="C16 Density within & between income">
  <div class="figure-title">C16 — Density Within & Between Income Groups</div>
  <div class="figure-meta">
    <span class="figure-badge badge-hero">★★★ Hero</span>
    <span class="figure-script">R/fig-burden-mismatch.R (paper fig 3)</span>
  </div>
  <div class="figure-description">Studies per capita × income, dot strip. Is the gap between income groups, or within them?</div>
  <div class="figure-finding">Both: between-group gap is large (17.8× median), but within-group spread (50–141×) dwarfs between-group spread. Some LMICs outperform many HICs.</div>
</div>

<div class="figure-card">
  <img src="../figures/fig_top_producers.png" alt="C17 Top producers">
  <div class="figure-title">C17 — Top Producers: Volume vs Per-Capita</div>
  <div class="figure-meta">
    <span class="figure-badge badge-solid">★★ Solid</span>
    <span class="figure-script">R/fig-top-producers.R</span>
  </div>
  <div class="figure-description">Two-rank slope chart (log axis): who leads by count vs by output per person.</div>
  <div class="figure-finding">USA/UK/China lead by volume; small wealthy countries (Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland) lead per-capita. Different leaders for different metrics.</div>
</div>

<div class="figure-card">
  <img src="../figures/fig_authorship_pattern.png" alt="C18 Authorship pattern">
  <div class="figure-title">C18 — Who Leads Research About Each Setting</div>
  <div class="figure-meta">
    <span class="figure-badge badge-hero">★★★ Hero</span>
    <span class="figure-script">R/fig-authorship-pattern.R</span>
  </div>
  <div class="figure-description">Stacked bars: local only / local+foreign / foreign only, by income group of country studied. Extracted geography only.</div>
  <div class="figure-finding"><strong>28% of low-income country studies have NO local author.</strong> Foreign-only dominates LIC; HIC research is mostly local. Parachute research visible in the data.</div>
</div>

<div class="figure-card">
  <img src="../figures/fig_collab_chord.png" alt="C19 Collaboration chord">
  <div class="figure-title">C19 — Income-Group Collaboration Structure (Chord)</div>
  <div class="figure-meta">
    <span class="figure-badge badge-solid">★★ Solid</span>
    <span class="figure-script">R/fig-companion-collab.R</span>
  </div>
  <div class="figure-description">Chord diagram: cross-income co-authorship of 32,731 eligible studies. Self-loops (within-group) excluded from ribbons.</div>
  <div class="figure-finding"><strong>High-income teams are the hub.</strong> 24,162 wholly HIC studies vs 37 wholly LIC. Every income group connects mainly through HIC. Cross-income collaboration is HIC-mediated.</div>
</div>

<div class="figure-card">
  <img src="../figures/fig_equity_time.png" alt="T1 Equity over time">
  <div class="figure-title">T1 — Equity Over Time</div>
  <div class="figure-meta">
    <span class="figure-badge badge-timeline">Timeline</span>
    <span class="figure-script">R/fig-companion-equity-time.R</span>
  </div>
  <div class="figure-description">LMIC share of annual single-country output vs their burden share (2010–2025). Is research attention shifting toward need?</div>
  <div class="figure-finding">Rose **16% → 36%** (2010→2025) — real progress, yet still far below **83% LMIC burden share** (dashed line). Shaded band = distance to burden-proportional reference.</div>
</div>

<div class="figure-card">
  <img src="../figures/fig_qaly_time.png" alt="T2 QALY-metric convergence">
  <div class="figure-title">T2 — QALY-Metric Convergence by Income</div>
  <div class="figure-meta">
    <span class="figure-badge badge-timeline">Timeline</span>
    <span class="figure-script">R/fig-companion-qaly-time.R</span>
  </div>
  <div class="figure-description">QALY use by income group over time. The metric gap over time.</div>
  <div class="figure-finding">LMIC **15% → 49%** vs HIC **51% → 59%** (2010→2025). Gap narrowed ~10pp but persists. LMIC catching up on comparable metric adoption.</div>
</div>

<div class="figure-card">
  <img src="../figures/fig_reach_time.png" alt="T3 Reach over time">
  <div class="figure-title">T3 — Reach Over Time</div>
  <div class="figure-meta">
    <span class="figure-badge badge-timeline">Timeline</span>
    <span class="figure-script">R/fig-companion-reach-time.R</span>
  </div>
  <div class="figure-description">Cumulative % of each income group's countries with ≥1 evaluation. Country universe denominators per income group.</div>
  <div class="figure-finding">HIC covered early; LIC reached last (**28% → 96%**). Geographic reach expanding but uneven — LIC coverage only recently approaching saturation.</div>
</div>
